questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of recruitment?
questions.explanation: Recruitment exists to fill open positions with suitable candidates; payroll, sales and facilities belong to other functions.

questions.question_text: A company has three vacancies for customer support executives. Which activity best describes what recruitment will do?
questions.explanation: Filling vacancies with suitable candidates is the core purpose of recruitment.

questions.question_text: Recruitment quality directly affects the quality of the workforce a business builds.
questions.explanation: Every hire becomes part of the workforce, so the quality of recruitment shapes team performance.

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly reflects the recruitment lifecycle?
questions.explanation: The lifecycle starts with understanding the requirement and ends with the candidate joining.

questions.question_text: What should be Kavya's first step in the recruitment lifecycle?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Kavya has just received a new requirement for an Accounts Executive at the fictional firm Nilgiri Foods.
questions.explanation: Every recruitment cycle begins by understanding the requirement; sourcing without it wastes effort.

questions.question_text: Which lifecycle stage comes next for Arjun?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Arjun has cleared the screening call. The hiring manager has reviewed his profile and asked to meet him on Thursday.
questions.explanation: After screening and profile approval, the next stage is the interview.

questions.question_text: Which lifecycle stage comes next for Meera?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Meera attended her final interview yesterday. The client has confirmed in writing that she is selected.
questions.explanation: Once selection is confirmed, the next stage is the offer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are core responsibilities of a recruiter? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Recruiters own requirement understanding, screening and coordination; budget approval sits with leadership.

questions.question_text: Recruiter Sameer supports a new hiring drive. Which tasks belong to his role? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Sourcing, communication and records are recruiter tasks; salary policy is a management decision.

questions.question_text: Who usually makes the final hiring decision for a candidate?
questions.explanation: The recruiter supports and advises, but the hiring manager or client makes the final decision.

questions.question_text: What is the most professional action?
questions.scenario_text: A hiring manager asks recruiter Divya to send ten profiles by evening. Divya has found only four candidates who meet the mandatory requirements.
questions.explanation: Quality and honesty come first: share suitable profiles and communicate the gap transparently.

questions.question_text: What does 'notice period' mean in recruitment?
questions.explanation: Notice period is the contractual time an employee must serve before leaving the current job.

questions.question_text: A candidate says, 'I have to serve 60 days before I can leave my current company.' Which term describes this?
questions.explanation: The time owed to the current employer before leaving is the notice period.

questions.question_text: What is a 'pipeline' in recruitment?
questions.explanation: The pipeline shows candidates and the stage each one is at for a requirement.

questions.question_text: CTC (Cost to Company) refers to the total annual cost an employer bears for an employee, not only the in-hand monthly salary.
questions.explanation: CTC includes salary and other employer-borne components; in-hand pay is usually lower.

questions.question_text: Which candidate should be prioritised?
questions.scenario_text: A requirement states: 'Sales Executive, 2–4 years of field sales experience, Pune, two-wheeler with valid licence mandatory.'
questions.explanation: Rahul meets the experience, location and mandatory two-wheeler requirement.

questions.question_text: Which candidate should be prioritised?
questions.scenario_text: A requirement states: 'Warehouse Supervisor, 3–5 years in warehouse operations, Chennai, rotational shifts mandatory.'
questions.explanation: Karthik matches experience, location and the mandatory shift requirement.

questions.question_text: A requirement is unclear about whether a graduation degree is mandatory. What should the recruiter do?
questions.explanation: Unclear requirements must be clarified with the hiring manager, not assumed.

questions.question_text: Which is the most professional way to begin a call with a candidate?
questions.explanation: A clear introduction and checking availability shows respect and sets a professional tone.

questions.question_text: Recruiter Asha calls candidate Vikram for the first time. What should she say first?
questions.explanation: Opening with identity, purpose and a permission check is the professional standard.

questions.question_text: What is the best response?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Farhan emails asking about the status of his application. The client has not yet shared feedback.
questions.explanation: Timely, honest updates with a next-update date keep trust without inventing outcomes.

questions.question_text: It is acceptable to stop responding to a candidate once they are no longer being considered.
questions.explanation: Candidates should be informed politely of the outcome; silence damages the employer and recruiter reputation.

questions.question_text: A candidate shares their current salary in confidence. What is the ethical approach?
questions.explanation: Candidate information is confidential and used only for its intended recruitment purpose.

questions.question_text: Recruiter Nikhil holds resumes of candidates for a client requirement. A friend asks for those resumes for an unrelated business. What should Nikhil do?
questions.explanation: Candidate data must not be shared outside the authorised recruitment purpose.

questions.question_text: What is the most appropriate action?
questions.scenario_text: A hiring manager tells recruiter Ritu to avoid candidates above a certain age even though age has no bearing on the job.
questions.explanation: Discrimination on non-job criteria is unethical; the recruiter should push back and escalate.

questions.question_text: What is the most appropriate action?
questions.scenario_text: A client asks recruiter Joseph to share only candidates from a particular religion for a data-entry role.
questions.explanation: Religion is not a job-related criterion; the request must be declined and escalated.

questions.question_text: A recruiter may change a candidate's experience on the resume to make the profile look stronger.
questions.explanation: Altering candidate information is dishonest and a serious breach of professional conduct.

questions.question_text: Which activity is usually best done at the start of a recruiter's day?
questions.explanation: Starting with pending actions and priorities keeps the day organised and nothing is missed.

questions.question_text: What should Lakshmi do first?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Lakshmi has three interviews to confirm, five follow-ups and one new requirement today.
questions.explanation: Time-sensitive items such as same-day interviews come first, followed by planned work.

questions.question_text: Updating candidate status at the end of each day helps keep the pipeline accurate.
questions.explanation: Daily updates keep records reliable and make reporting accurate.

questions.question_text: Which habits support an effective recruiter daily workflow? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Prioritising, prompt recording and dated follow-ups keep work organised; delaying updates causes errors.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of a Job Description (JD)?
questions.explanation: A JD defines the role and requirements, guiding sourcing and screening.

questions.question_text: A recruiter receives a JD for a Data Analyst role. How should the JD be used?
questions.explanation: The JD is the reference for every recruitment decision on that role.

questions.question_text: Which sections are commonly found in a JD? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Title, responsibilities and requirements are standard JD sections; bank details are not.

questions.question_text: What kind of role is this in practice?
questions.scenario_text: JD title: 'Business Development Executive'. Responsibilities: cold-calling prospects, field visits, closing new client deals.
questions.explanation: Responsibilities reveal the real role: this is new-client sales despite the general title.

questions.question_text: What kind of role is this in practice?
questions.scenario_text: JD title: 'Associate – Operations'. Responsibilities: processing insurance claims, verifying documents, updating the claims system.
questions.explanation: The title is generic; the responsibilities show it is claims processing.

questions.question_text: Two companies can use the same job title for roles with very different responsibilities.
questions.explanation: Titles vary between companies, so recruiters must read responsibilities to understand the role.

questions.question_text: A JD lists 'Tally ERP – must have' and 'GST filing – good to have'. How should the recruiter treat these?
questions.explanation: 'Must have' marks a mandatory requirement; 'good to have' marks a preferred one.

questions.question_text: A JD states 'Excel – mandatory' and 'Power BI – added advantage'. A candidate knows Power BI but not Excel. What is the right assessment?
questions.explanation: A preferred skill cannot compensate for a missing mandatory skill.

questions.question_text: How should Sneha be classified?
questions.scenario_text: JD for a Customer Support Associate: 'Fluent English and Hindi – mandatory; prior BPO experience – preferred.' Candidate Sneha is fluent in both languages, a fresher with no BPO experience.
questions.explanation: Mandatory criteria are met; a missing preferred item does not disqualify her.

questions.question_text: How should Rohan be classified?
questions.scenario_text: JD for an Inventory Executive: 'SAP MM – mandatory; warehouse experience – preferred.' Candidate Rohan has 3 years of warehouse experience but no SAP MM.
questions.explanation: The mandatory SAP MM requirement is missing; preferred experience cannot replace it.

questions.question_text: A JD requires 'B.Com or M.Com'. Which candidate meets the qualification?
questions.explanation: Only the B.Com holder matches the stated qualification.

questions.question_text: Which skills are required? Select all that apply.
questions.scenario_text: JD for a Junior Web Developer: 'HTML, CSS and JavaScript required; React preferred.'
questions.explanation: HTML, CSS and JavaScript are required; React is preferred, not required.

questions.question_text: Which skills are required? Select all that apply.
questions.scenario_text: JD for an HR Executive: 'Payroll processing, statutory compliance (PF/ESI) and MS Excel required; HRMS experience preferred.'
questions.explanation: Payroll, compliance and Excel are required; HRMS is preferred.

questions.question_text: How much relevant experience does Anil have for this JD?
questions.scenario_text: JD requires '3–5 years of experience in B2B sales'. Candidate Anil has 7 years total: 4 years in B2B sales and 3 years in retail store management.
questions.explanation: Only the B2B sales experience is relevant to this requirement.

questions.question_text: How much relevant experience does Priya have for this JD?
questions.scenario_text: JD requires '2–3 years in accounts payable'. Candidate Priya has 5 years total: 2 years in accounts payable and 3 years in front-office administration.
questions.explanation: Relevant experience counts only the accounts payable years.

questions.question_text: Total years of experience and relevant years of experience always mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: Relevant experience counts only work that matches the requirement; total experience can include unrelated roles.

questions.question_text: A JD says 'Work mode: Hybrid – 3 days in office, Hyderabad'. Which candidate fits best?
questions.explanation: Hybrid in Hyderabad requires regular office attendance there.

questions.question_text: A JD says 'Work from office, Noida, 5 days a week'. Which candidate fits best?
questions.explanation: The role needs full-time office attendance in Noida.

questions.question_text: What should the recruiter conclude?
questions.scenario_text: A JD requires 'night shift (10 PM–7 AM) for US clients'. Candidate Arvind matches all skills but says he can only work day shifts.
questions.explanation: Shift timing is a stated requirement; not meeting it makes the profile unsuitable unless the client agrees.

questions.question_text: A JD states a budget of up to ₹6 LPA. A candidate's current CTC is ₹5.5 LPA and expectation is ₹9 LPA. What should the recruiter do?
questions.explanation: Salary gaps must be identified and discussed openly before submission.

questions.question_text: A role has a budget of ₹4–5 LPA. Candidate Zoya expects ₹4.8 LPA. How should her expectation be assessed?
questions.explanation: ₹4.8 LPA falls within the ₹4–5 LPA range.

questions.question_text: A client needs someone to join within 15 days. Candidate Manoj has a 90-day notice period with no buyout option. What is the correct assessment?
questions.explanation: A 90-day notice period cannot meet a 15-day joining requirement.

questions.question_text: Which items should be converted from a JD into a candidate profile before sourcing? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A candidate profile captures job-related requirements, not personal preferences.

questions.question_text: Recruiter Gautam is building a candidate profile from a JD for a Logistics Coordinator. What should it include? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Only job-related requirements belong in a candidate profile.

questions.question_text: Before sourcing for a new JD, which screening points are most important to note?
questions.explanation: Key screening points are the job-related requirements that determine suitability.

questions.question_text: What should the recruiter do?
questions.scenario_text: A JD says 'Experience in ERP systems'. It does not name which ERP.
questions.explanation: When a requirement is vague, the recruiter should clarify it rather than assume.

questions.question_text: What should the recruiter do?
questions.scenario_text: A JD for a Field Technician says 'travel required' without saying how much or where.
questions.explanation: Clarifying the travel expectation avoids mismatches later in the process.

questions.question_text: Asking the hiring manager to clarify an unclear requirement is a sign of a professional recruiter.
questions.explanation: Clarifying early prevents wasted sourcing and wrong submissions.

questions.question_text: In which JD section would a recruiter normally find the daily tasks of the role?
questions.explanation: Daily tasks are described under responsibilities.

questions.question_text: What is candidate sourcing?
questions.explanation: Sourcing is the activity of finding and identifying potential candidates.

questions.question_text: Recruiter Harsh is searching job boards and referrals for candidates who fit a new requirement. Which activity is he doing?
questions.explanation: Searching for potential candidates is sourcing.

questions.question_text: Which of these are valid candidate sourcing channels? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Referrals, job portals and the internal database are legitimate channels; using contacts without consent is not.

questions.question_text: Which sourcing approach is most suitable?
questions.scenario_text: A requirement needs 25 entry-level warehouse associates in Bhiwandi within two weeks.
questions.explanation: Volume entry-level hiring in a local area suits walk-ins and local referrals.

questions.question_text: Which sourcing approach is most suitable?
questions.scenario_text: A requirement needs one senior Treasury Manager with 15 years of experience.
questions.explanation: Senior niche roles need targeted, network-based sourcing.

questions.question_text: Before starting to source for a new requirement, what should a sourcing strategy define first?
questions.explanation: A sourcing strategy starts with who to target, where and how.

questions.question_text: What should her sourcing strategy include?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Nisha has a new requirement for Python developers in Bengaluru.
questions.explanation: A strategy defines the target, channels, search keywords and goals.

questions.question_text: The same sourcing channel works equally well for every type of role.
questions.explanation: Channel effectiveness depends on role level, location and volume.

questions.question_text: In Boolean search, what does AND do?
questions.explanation: AND narrows the search by requiring every term.

questions.question_text: A recruiter searches: Java AND Spring. Which profiles are returned?
questions.explanation: AND requires both terms to appear.

questions.question_text: In Boolean search, what does OR do?
questions.explanation: OR broadens the search to include any of the terms, useful for synonyms.

questions.question_text: Which search finds profiles mentioning either 'accountant' or 'accounts executive'?
questions.explanation: OR returns profiles that include either term.

questions.question_text: A recruiter wants sales profiles but not internships. Which search is correct?
questions.explanation: NOT excludes profiles containing the specified term.

questions.question_text: A recruiter wants nursing profiles but wants to exclude trainee profiles. Which search is correct?
questions.explanation: NOT removes profiles containing 'trainee'.

questions.question_text: Why are quotation marks used in a search such as "customer service"?
questions.explanation: Quotation marks keep the words together as an exact phrase.

questions.question_text: Which Boolean search is correct?
questions.scenario_text: A recruiter needs candidates with Java or Python who also know SQL.
questions.explanation: Brackets group the alternatives so that SQL is required with either language.

questions.question_text: Which Boolean search is correct?
questions.scenario_text: A recruiter needs accountants or auditors based in Pune.
questions.explanation: Brackets make Pune apply to both alternatives.

questions.question_text: Which keywords are useful for sourcing a 'Recruitment Executive'? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Synonyms and related terms widen relevant results; unrelated terms add noise.

questions.question_text: How relevant is Ravi's profile?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: Customer Support, 1–3 years in voice process, English fluency, Bengaluru. Candidate Ravi: 2 years in voice process, fluent English, lives in Bengaluru.
questions.explanation: Ravi meets all mandatory requirements.

questions.question_text: How relevant is Sana's profile?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: Graphic Designer, 2+ years, Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop, Mumbai. Candidate Sana: 3 years, Illustrator and Photoshop, lives in Mumbai.
questions.explanation: Sana meets all stated requirements.

questions.question_text: How should Deepa's profile be classified?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: Accounts Executive, 2–4 years, Tally mandatory, Chennai. Candidate Deepa: 3 years in accounts, uses Busy software (not Tally), Chennai.
questions.explanation: Deepa matches most requirements but lacks the mandatory tool, making her a partial match.

questions.question_text: How should Vivek's profile be classified?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: Field Sales, 2–4 years, FMCG, Jaipur. Candidate Vivek: 3 years in pharma field sales, Jaipur.
questions.explanation: Vivek has relevant field sales experience but not the industry, so he is a partial match.

questions.question_text: How should Omkar's profile be classified?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: Senior Java Developer, 6+ years. Candidate Omkar: 1 year in manual testing.
questions.explanation: Omkar lacks both the skill and experience required.

questions.question_text: Recording the source of each candidate helps measure which channels work best.
questions.explanation: Source tracking shows channel effectiveness and avoids ownership disputes.

questions.question_text: Which details should be recorded when a candidate is sourced? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Factual sourcing details keep records useful; personal opinions about appearance are inappropriate.

questions.question_text: Before moving a sourced candidate to screening, what should the recruiter prepare?
questions.explanation: Screening preparation identifies matching points and items to clarify.

questions.question_text: What should she prepare?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Tanvi has shortlisted five sourced profiles for screening calls tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Preparing verification points for each profile makes screening focused and consistent.

questions.question_text: Which is the best structure for a candidate sourcing plan?
questions.explanation: A sourcing plan covers what to look for, where, how and how progress is tracked.

questions.question_text: A sourcing plan should be reviewed and adjusted if a channel is not producing suitable candidates.
questions.explanation: Plans should adapt based on results.

questions.question_text: What is a key benefit of employee referrals as a sourcing channel?
questions.explanation: Referrals can give useful context, but candidates still need normal screening.

questions.question_text: Which message is the most professional way to contact a candidate about a role?
questions.explanation: A professional message introduces the recruiter, the role and respects the candidate's time.

questions.question_text: Recruiter Manish needs to message candidate Kiran about an opening. Which message is best?
questions.explanation: Clear identity, role details and a polite request make the message professional.

questions.question_text: Using a polite, clear and respectful tone is part of professional candidate communication.
questions.explanation: Tone shapes how candidates perceive the recruiter and employer.

questions.question_text: Which order best reflects a structured screening call?
questions.explanation: A structured call opens properly, verifies fit, invites questions and confirms next steps.

questions.question_text: How should she close the call?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Pallavi is preparing her screening call with candidate Sunil.
questions.explanation: Closing with a summary and clear next steps keeps the candidate informed.

questions.question_text: Which items should a recruiter verify during a screening call? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Verify job-related information; personal details such as marital status are not relevant.

questions.question_text: Which screening question is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Questions must relate to the job requirements.

questions.question_text: Which screening question is appropriate for a Field Sales role?
questions.explanation: Field visits are a job requirement; the other questions are personal and inappropriate.

questions.question_text: What is the best follow-up question?
questions.scenario_text: The JD requires SAP FICO experience. Candidate Rekha says she has 'worked on SAP'.
questions.explanation: A specific, open question verifies whether the experience matches the requirement.

questions.question_text: What screening decision fits?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: 2–4 years in inside sales, English and Hindi, Gurugram. Candidate Ajay: 3 years inside sales, fluent in both, lives in Gurugram.
questions.explanation: All requirements are met, so the decision is Match.

questions.question_text: What screening decision fits?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: 1–2 years in payroll, Excel, Ahmedabad. Candidate Hetal: 2 years in payroll, advanced Excel, lives in Ahmedabad.
questions.explanation: Hetal meets every requirement.

questions.question_text: What screening decision fits?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: GST return filing mandatory. Candidate Naveen's resume mentions 'taxation work' but not GST specifically.
questions.explanation: The information is unclear, so it must be clarified before deciding.

questions.question_text: What screening decision fits?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: valid forklift licence mandatory. Candidate Babu mentions 'warehouse equipment handling' without saying whether he holds a licence.
questions.explanation: Licence status is unknown, so it must be clarified.

questions.question_text: How should this be recorded?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: 3–5 years, Python mandatory, Bengaluru. Candidate Sowmya: 4 years in Python, Bengaluru, but expects ₹2 LPA above the maximum budget.
questions.explanation: Skills match but a specific gap exists; recording it transparently lets the client decide.

questions.question_text: How should this be recorded?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: join within 30 days. Candidate Rohit matches all skills but has a 60-day notice period, negotiable to 45.
questions.explanation: The notice period is a known, specific gap that the hiring manager should evaluate.

questions.question_text: What screening decision fits?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: licensed pharmacist (mandatory) for a hospital pharmacy. Candidate Ali has hospital store experience but no pharmacist registration.
questions.explanation: A mandatory legal qualification is missing, so the candidate is not suitable.

questions.question_text: Screening decisions should be based on evidence against the requirement, not on a candidate's appearance or background.
questions.explanation: Evidence-based, job-related evaluation is fair and professional.

questions.question_text: What is the best response?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Megha asks about the salary range before agreeing to an interview. The recruiter has an approved budget range.
questions.explanation: Honest, approved information builds trust and avoids drop-outs later.

questions.question_text: What is the best response?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Sandeep asks whether the role involves weekend work. The JD says one Saturday per month.
questions.explanation: Accurate answers prevent mismatched expectations.

questions.question_text: What is the most professional way to handle this objection?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Lavanya says, 'The commute to the office is too long for me.'
questions.explanation: Objections are handled with empathy and facts, never pressure or misinformation.

questions.question_text: When a candidate raises a concern you cannot answer, it is better to give an approximate answer than to say you will check.
questions.explanation: Commit to checking and follow up; guessing creates wrong expectations.

questions.question_text: Which information must an interview confirmation include?
questions.explanation: Complete confirmation details prevent missed or delayed interviews.

questions.question_text: What should her confirmation include?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Usha is confirming a face-to-face interview for candidate Prakash.
questions.explanation: Clear logistics help the candidate arrive on time and prepared.

questions.question_text: What should Faisal do first?
questions.scenario_text: An interview is scheduled for 11 AM. At 9 AM, the client informs recruiter Faisal that the interviewer is unavailable.
questions.explanation: Prompt, respectful communication of changes protects the candidate experience.

questions.question_text: Which steps help reduce interview no-shows? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Clear confirmation and reminders reduce no-shows; withholding details increases them.

questions.question_text: A candidate attended an interview three days ago and feedback is still pending. What should the recruiter do?
questions.explanation: Regular updates and chasing feedback keep the process moving and the candidate informed.

questions.question_text: How should the recruiter communicate this?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Shreya was not selected after her final interview.
questions.explanation: Respectful, honest closure maintains professionalism.

questions.question_text: Screening notes should record facts such as experience, CTC and notice period rather than personal opinions.
questions.explanation: Factual notes are reliable and fair.

questions.question_text: After a screening call, when should the recruiter update the candidate record?
questions.explanation: Prompt updates keep records accurate and useful to others.

questions.question_text: Which next steps are correct, in order?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Imran has cleared screening. The client wants to interview him this week.
questions.explanation: The coordination workflow moves from submission through scheduling to feedback.

questions.question_text: What is the correct coordination sequence?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Nandini has been shortlisted by the client after screening.
questions.explanation: Scheduling, confirmation, reminder and feedback follow-up is the correct order.

questions.question_text: Which field uniquely identifies a trainee or candidate record in a recruitment system?
questions.explanation: Names and cities repeat; a unique ID identifies one record.

questions.question_text: Two candidates are both named 'Rahul Sharma'. What keeps their records separate?
questions.explanation: Unique IDs and verified contact details prevent records being confused.

questions.question_text: Candidate status (for example, 'Interview Scheduled') is different from candidate notes.
questions.explanation: Status shows the pipeline stage; notes record what happened and why.

questions.question_text: What should Karan do?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Anjali informs recruiter Karan that her phone number has changed.
questions.explanation: Updating the existing record keeps one accurate history for the candidate.

questions.question_text: Which resume file name is most professional?
questions.explanation: A consistent naming convention makes documents easy to find and attribute.

questions.question_text: Which file name best follows a professional naming convention?
questions.explanation: Name, role and document type make the file identifiable.

questions.question_text: Which practices protect candidate documents? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Approved storage, authorised sharing and version control protect candidate data.

questions.question_text: What should the recruiter do?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Faizan sends an updated resume two weeks after his first one.
questions.explanation: Keeping all documents on one record with clear versions avoids duplicates and confusion.

questions.question_text: Is this recording correct?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: B.Com, 2 years in accounts payable, Tally. Candidate Geeta: B.Com, 3 years in accounts payable, Tally. Recorded as 'Match'.
questions.explanation: Geeta meets each requirement, so 'Match' is accurate.

questions.question_text: How should his record be marked against the requirement?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement: Diploma in Mechanical, 2 years in CNC operation. Candidate Ramesh: Diploma in Mechanical, 2.5 years in CNC operation.
questions.explanation: Qualification and experience both meet the requirement.

questions.question_text: How should this be recorded?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Lata's resume shows an MBA but does not say whether it was full-time or distance learning. The client requires a full-time MBA.
questions.explanation: Missing information that affects eligibility must be clarified, not assumed.

questions.question_text: Which are valid candidate source values? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Every candidate's source should be recorded accurately.

questions.question_text: Who should own Mohan's record, and what should Vinay do?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Aditi sourced candidate Mohan on Monday. On Wednesday, recruiter Vinay contacts Mohan for the same requirement.
questions.explanation: Ownership follows the documented first source; checking records first avoids duplicate contact.

questions.question_text: What should Ankit do?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Salma added candidate Deepak to the database last week for a Pune requirement. Recruiter Ankit finds Deepak's profile on a job portal today.
questions.explanation: Ownership and record checks prevent conflicts and duplicate outreach.

questions.question_text: Which recruiter note is the most professional?
questions.explanation: Good notes are dated, factual and state the next action.

questions.question_text: Which note best records a follow-up call?
questions.explanation: Dated facts and a clear next action make notes useful.

questions.question_text: Recruiter notes may include personal opinions about a candidate's appearance.
questions.explanation: Notes must be factual and job-related.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely conclusion and action?
questions.scenario_text: Two records exist: 'Suresh K, 98xxxx1234, Chennai' and 'Suresh Kumar, 98xxxx1234, Chennai'.
questions.explanation: The same phone number and city strongly suggest a duplicate that should be verified.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely conclusion and action?
questions.scenario_text: Two records exist: 'Kavitha R, kavitha.r@mail.example, Kochi' and 'Kavitha Ramesh, kavitha.r@mail.example, Kochi'.
questions.explanation: Matching email and city indicate a likely duplicate to verify.

questions.question_text: What should the recruiter do?
questions.scenario_text: Two records are both named 'Pooja Singh' with different phone numbers, emails and cities.
questions.explanation: Names alone never justify a merge; identifying details must match.

questions.question_text: A recruiter is unsure whether two records belong to the same person. What should they do?
questions.explanation: Unclear duplicates should be verified or escalated, not guessed.

questions.question_text: Which pipeline stage comes immediately after 'Screened' when the candidate is approved to move forward?
questions.explanation: Screened candidates who fit are moved to Shortlisted.

questions.question_text: Which stage comes immediately after 'Offered'?
questions.explanation: After an offer is made, the next stage is Offer Accepted once the candidate accepts.

questions.question_text: What is his correct current stage?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Ishaan has completed screening and the client has approved his profile. The interview date is being finalised.
questions.explanation: The interview is not yet scheduled; he is Shortlisted.

questions.question_text: What is her correct current stage?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Bhavna's interview is confirmed for Friday at 3 PM.
questions.explanation: A confirmed interview date means Interview Scheduled.

questions.question_text: What is his correct current stage?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Tarun attended his interview yesterday. The client has not shared feedback yet.
questions.explanation: Without feedback, the accurate stage is Interview Attended.

questions.question_text: What is the most accurate status?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Reshma accepted the offer but did not report on her joining date and is not responding.
questions.explanation: A candidate who does not join after accepting is recorded as a dropout once confirmed.

questions.question_text: Which of these are closing or exception statuses rather than forward stages? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Rejected, Not Interested and No Response end or pause progress; Shortlisted is a forward stage.

questions.question_text: Which tracking fields help a recruiter manage pending actions? Choose the most complete set.
questions.explanation: Complete tracking fields make every pending action visible and owned.

questions.question_text: Which entry best shows her pending action?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Pranav is reviewing his tracker for candidate Sheetal.
questions.explanation: A clear pending action, owner and due date make follow-through possible.

questions.question_text: What should she do first?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Ruchi's tracker shows five candidates with follow-up dates that passed two days ago.
questions.explanation: Overdue follow-ups need action and recorded outcomes, not silent changes.

questions.question_text: What status should Varun have?
questions.scenario_text: The client's interviewer says on a call that candidate Varun 'did well', but no written confirmation of selection has arrived.
questions.explanation: Never mark Selected before authorised confirmation.

questions.question_text: What status should Nidhi have today?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Nidhi accepted her offer. Her joining date is next Monday and today is Thursday.
questions.explanation: Joined is recorded only after joining is confirmed.

questions.question_text: A status should be changed only when there is evidence that the candidate has reached that stage.
questions.explanation: Evidence-based updates keep the pipeline trustworthy.

questions.question_text: What is the appropriate next step?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Yash has not replied to three calls and two messages over five days about an interview slot.
questions.explanation: Documented attempts and a defined status keep the record accurate.

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly reflects the interview-to-joining follow-up?
questions.explanation: Each step depends on the previous one being confirmed.

questions.question_text: What is the next action?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Akash has been selected in writing by the client.
questions.explanation: After written selection, the next step is the offer.

questions.question_text: What should the recruiter do?
questions.scenario_text: Candidate Swati accepted an offer with joining on the 1st. On the 28th she has not confirmed her relieving from her current company.
questions.explanation: Pre-joining follow-up identifies risks early and keeps the client informed.

questions.question_text: Which steps help reduce dropouts between offer acceptance and joining? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Consistent engagement and clear logistics reduce dropouts.

questions.question_text: What should a recruiter's daily report contain?
questions.explanation: Reports must reflect real activity and be organised by requirement.

questions.question_text: Recruiter Gopal made 30 calls, scheduled 4 interviews and had 2 joinings confirmed today. How should he report?
questions.explanation: Accurate, requirement-wise reporting is the professional standard.

questions.question_text: It is acceptable to estimate numbers in a daily report if the actual figures are not handy.
questions.explanation: Reports must never contain fabricated or guessed numbers.

questions.question_text: What should she do?
questions.scenario_text: While preparing her report, recruiter Simran notices that two candidates are marked 'Interview Scheduled' in the tracker but their interviews were cancelled.
questions.explanation: Reports are only as accurate as the records; fix the records first.

questions.question_text: Which task is usually the highest priority for a recruiter in the morning?
questions.explanation: Same-day interviews and joinings are time-critical.

questions.question_text: Which should he handle first?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Rahul has: a joining today, an overdue client feedback chase, and new sourcing for a role due next week.
questions.explanation: Time-critical same-day events come before other work.

questions.question_text: How should Dev prioritise?
questions.scenario_text: A client escalates that feedback for three candidates has not been collected, while recruiter Dev also has ten routine follow-ups due today.
questions.explanation: Client escalations are urgent; routine work still needs completion the same day.

questions.question_text: How should she prioritise?
questions.scenario_text: Recruiter Meenal has one candidate who may drop out before tomorrow's joining, and several low-priority database clean-up tasks.
questions.explanation: Risks to an imminent joining are urgent.

questions.question_text: Categorising tasks as Urgent, High, Normal and Follow-up-later helps a recruiter plan the day.
questions.explanation: Clear categories help focus effort where it matters most.

questions.question_text: Which actions belong in an end-of-day routine? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Updating records, planning follow-ups and accurate reporting close the day properly.

questions.question_text: How many positions remain open, excluding the accepted offer?
questions.scenario_text: Requirement 'Customer Support – Kochi' needs 5 hires. 3 candidates have joined and 1 has an accepted offer.
questions.explanation: 5 − 3 joined − 1 accepted offer leaves 1 position still to fill.

questions.question_text: Recording the source of a candidate helps resolve recruiter ownership questions.
questions.explanation: Documented source and date establish ownership.

questions.question_text: What should the recruiter do?
questions.scenario_text: A client changes the experience range for a requirement during a phone call.
questions.explanation: Requirement changes should be confirmed in writing and recorded.
